Isabella M. Gambill serves as a member of the Sustainable Solutions Lab Board [1]. Professionally, she is the Assistant Director of Climate, Energy, & Resilience at A Better City [1]. In this role, she represents 130 member business organizations and works to advance equitable climate and clean energy policy at the city and state levels in Massachusetts [1]. Her work includes leading efforts on extreme heat, participating in various policy coalitions, and helping to staff the Commercial Real Estate Working Group of the Green Ribbon Commission (GRC) [1]. Additionally, Isabella serves on the following boards and committees:
* The Community Advisory Board for Boston’s 20-Year Urban Forest Plan [1]
* The Advisory Group for the GRC’s Climate Justice Initiative [1]
* The Steering Committee for a MA/Boston Climate Bank [1]
* The Board of Visitors and Young Leaders Council of Fenway Health [1] Prior to her current position, she worked as a Policy Officer for the United Nations’ Biodiversity Law and Governance Initiative and on domestic and international conservation networks with the Lincoln Institute of Land Policy [1]. Cassandre Rey-Thibault (Summer 2024)
Focus: risk prevention and crisis management, coastal urban territories
Bio: I am a postdoctoral researcher at the Centre for European Studies and Comparative Politics (CEE) at Sciences Po Paris, funded by the Bruno Latour Fund. I hold a PhD in geography, specializing in risk prevention and crisis management policies in French urban areas. My research compares risk governance in coastal urban territories in the context of climate change, examining the evolution and limitations of traditional risk management paradigms. In coastal urban areas such as Boston, knowledge production and risk management practices must evolve to address their interactions and combinations. At SSL, I conducted research interviews and studied the evolution of risk governance in the metropolitan area and assisted the SSL team in fostering collaborative research on climate social resilience in Boston.
